chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmud, who said:
I heard Al-Reza (peace be upon him) saying: 'One should perform istinja (cleansing) and wash what is apparent from it upon the anus, and the finger should not be inserted into it.'

key_terms.يُسْتَنْجَى: Istinja: Cleansing oneself from excrement using water

ai.seo_question: What is the correct method for washing after defecation according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the fiqh of istinja by distinguishing between external washing and internal insertion, noting that while the visible area must be washed, the finger (anmulah) should not be inserted deeply into the rectum. This ruling reflects the scholarly consensus on avoiding unnecessary intrusion while ensuring purity, balancing ritual cleanliness with physical comfort. It serves as a practical guideline for daily hygiene within the framework of Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibrahim Bin Abu Mahmoud who said,
‘I heard Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘One should cleanse and wash what is apparent from it upon the anus, and you should not enter the finger inside it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibrahim ibn abu Mahmud who has said

the following: “I heard abu al-Hassan, al-Rida, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘One should get rid of remaining feces and urine by washing what is outside of the buttocks and there is no need to enter one’s fingers inside.’”
